lines.japanese: メンマの店を覗くと、若草色のド派手なスーツがカウンター席に座っていた。美形のスカウトマン、プラチナだ。
lines.english: When I looked in at Menma's, an outrageously bright spring-green suit occupied one of the counter seats. Platinum, the handsome scout.

lines.japanese: 「うす」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、ドラさーん！」
lines.english: “Ah, Dra!”

lines.japanese: 隣りに腰を下ろすと、男前の甘いマスクがひと懐っこく破顔する。しかしよく見ると、左の頬が赤く腫れていて、唇には切り傷があった。しょーもねえ、誰かとケンカでもしたんだろう。
lines.english: I took the seat beside him, and his handsome, sweet-featured face broke into a friendly smile. Looking closer, though, I saw his left cheek was red and swollen and his lip split. Pathetic. Another fight, probably.

lines.japanese: しかしやつはそんな軽傷など忘れているみたいで、店主に新しいコップを要求し、それをドカンと俺の前に置いた。
lines.english: He seemed to have forgotten the minor injuries. He demanded a fresh cup from the proprietor and planted it with a thump before me.

lines.japanese: 「まーまー、駆けつけ一杯。僕のおごりっすよ」
lines.english: “Come on, first drink of the night. My treat.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、悪い、俺はちょっと……」
lines.english: “Ah, sorry. I don't really—”

lines.japanese: やつはほろ酔いのご機嫌顔で、ぬる燗の日本酒を注いだ。俺は≪取り決め≫によってアルコールの摂取を禁じられているが、なんだかここは遠慮しづらい雰囲気だった。
lines.english: Beaming in the first glow of drink, he poured gently warmed sake into the cup. The *Agreement* forbade me alcohol, but the mood made it difficult to refuse.

lines.japanese: 「つか、なんだよ気持ち悪ぃな、殴られてるくせにニヤニヤして。なんかいいことでもあったの」
lines.english: “What's with that creepy grin when somebody's punched you in the face? Something good happen?”

lines.japanese: 「いいことー？　へへー、どうでしょうねー。やー、あるといいなあ、いいこと！」
lines.english: “Something good? Heh heh. Who knows? Sure hope something does!”

lines.japanese: プラチナはすでに出来あがってるんだろうか、優雅な王子様キャラの仮面は外れ、コンパ用の軽薄なチャラ男に変貌していた。俺はシラフの角刈りに目配せをした。
lines.english: Was Platinum already drunk? The elegant-prince mask had come off, leaving the frivolous playboy he became on group dates. I sent a meaningful look toward the sober crew cut.

lines.japanese: 「こいつ、今日は酔う前からこんななんだ」
lines.english: “He's been like this since before he started drinking.”

lines.japanese: メンマはそう言いながら、さりげなく俺の前にふたつめのコップを置いた。透明の液体が入ってる。俺はそっちを軽く口に含んだ。無味無臭。ただの水だ。なかなか気配りの行きとどく店主じゃないか。
lines.english: As he spoke, Menma casually set a second cup before me. Clear liquid. I took a small sip: no taste, no smell. Water. The proprietor knew how to look after people.

lines.japanese: 「おっさん、俺いつもの」
lines.english: “Old man, the usual.”

lines.japanese: 俺はいちばん安いラーメンを注文して、ぺらぺらと昔語りを続けるプラチナの方へ気持ち体を向けた。
lines.english: I ordered the cheapest ramen and turned myself slightly toward Platinum, who was rattling on about the old days.

lines.japanese: 「ドラさん僕ね、自慢じゃないすけどね、映画出たことあんすよ映画。ＡＶじゃないっすよ、普通の映画っすよ。映ってんの後ろ姿ばっかすけどね、いちおー台詞もあったんすよ、ふたつ」
lines.english: “Dra, not to brag, but I've been in a movie. A movie! Not porn, a regular movie. Mostly the back of my head, sure, but I had two actual lines.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、マジだー、良かったなー」
lines.english: “Oh, wow. Good for you.”

lines.japanese: プラチナは語り上戸だ。ろれつが回らないほどには酔ってないから、べつに声そのものが耳障りってわけではないんだけど、難を言えばこれがすでに何度も聞かされている話だってこと。
lines.english: Platinum was a storytelling drunk. He wasn't slurring yet, so his voice itself wasn't unpleasant. The trouble was, I'd heard this story several times already.

lines.japanese: 「ドラさん！　いいすか！」
lines.english: “Dra! Listen to me!”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　おお、なんだよ」
lines.english: “Huh? Sure. What?”

lines.japanese: 「あのね！　僕はなにも、汁男とかスカウトやるために田舎から出てきたわけじゃないんすよ！」
lines.english: “Listen! I didn't come all the way from the sticks to be a cum-shot extra or a talent scout!”

lines.japanese: プラチナが生まれたのは、温泉街で有名な盆地の町だ。日本地図で見ると西の端の方。
lines.english: Platinum had been born in a basin town famous for its hot springs, over near the western edge of Japan.

lines.japanese: 駅の観光案内パンフで見たときは、もうもうと湯気（霧じゃなくて湯気！）が立ちのぼる珍しい湖や、緑なす田園地帯を行くのどかな辻馬車が紹介されていた。俺も金さえあれば一度は行ってみたいと思ったぐらいだ。
lines.english: The tourist brochure at the station showed an unusual lake billowing steam—not mist, steam!—and placid horse-drawn carriages crossing lush green farmland. It had made even me want to visit, if I ever found the money.

lines.japanese: やつは義務教育課程を修了すると、親族一同の反対を押しきり家出同然（ていうか家出そのものだ）で柳木原へやってきた。
lines.english: Once he finished his compulsory education, he defied his entire family and ran off to Yanagihara, practically running away from home (actually, he straight-up ran away).

lines.japanese: 何年か芝居の勉強をしながら働いて金を溜め、いずれはハリウッドスターを目指してステイツへ飛ぶつもりだったらしい。
lines.english: Apparently he meant to work and save while studying acting for a few years, then fly to the States and pursue Hollywood stardom.

lines.japanese: 「ま、そこはほら、なんせ可愛いガキの考えることっすから」
lines.english: “Well, you know. It was the sort of thing a cute little kid dreams up.”

lines.japanese: やつはいつもここで片手を頭の後ろに置いて、はにかむように笑う。
lines.english: Here he always put one hand behind his head and smiled shyly.

lines.japanese: しかし、公園のベンチやビルの軒先で野宿しながら三日間仕事を探しまわったが、年齢を偽ってるのが明らかな家出少年など、どこへ行っても門前払いだ。
lines.english: But after three days of sleeping on park benches and beneath the eaves of buildings while hunting for work, an obvious underage runaway lying about his age had been turned away from every door.

lines.japanese: 四日目に歓楽街の奥の奥へ踏みこみ、少年趣味のマダムが訪れる小さな地下クラブでようやく職にありつけた。
lines.english: On the fourth day, he ventured into the deepest reaches of the entertainment district and finally found work at a little basement club patronized by wealthy women with a taste for boys.

lines.japanese: アメリカンドリーム（の足がかり）を掴むため、夢見る少年はホールでキッチンで真摯に働いた。まめやかで人当たりがよく相手を立てる才にも秀でたプラチナに、ホストの仕事は天職だった。
lines.english: To grasp his American dream—or at least its first rung—the dreaming boy worked earnestly in the dining room and the kitchen. Attentive, charming, and exceptionally gifted at making others feel important, Platinum had found his calling as a host.

lines.japanese: 最初のひと月は三食をパンの耳で凌いだりもしたらしいが、半年も経つころにはもう人並みの生活が送れる程度の収入を勝ちえていた。
lines.english: For his first month, he supposedly survived on three meals of bread crusts a day. Within six months, he had secured enough income to live like an ordinary person.

lines.japanese: 「思えばあのころが、僕の人生でいちばん真面目な時期だったなあ。だってね、夜の仕事を隠しながら、昼は役者の卵としてちゃんとレッスンとかオーディションに取りくんでたわけですよ？　根性あったなあ自分」
lines.english: “Looking back, that was the most serious period of my life. Think about it: I hid my night job while spending my days properly taking lessons and auditioning as an aspiring actor. I had guts back then.”

lines.japanese: しかし夜の収入が増えるにつれ、昼の生活はおろそかになっていった。女の電話番号が増えるにつれ、夢への情熱は失われていった。
lines.english: But as his nighttime income rose, he neglected his daytime life. As women's phone numbers multiplied, his passion for the dream dwindled.

lines.japanese: そして季節が何度か巡り、恋愛観と経済観念が狂いはじめたころ。稼ぎ頭として調子に乗っていたプラチナは、恨みや僻みを抱いた同僚たちの黒い策略にはまり店を追放されてしまう。
lines.english: Several seasons passed. His ideas about love and money began to warp. Riding high as the club's top earner, Platinum fell victim to the dark machinations of colleagues nursing jealousy and resentment and was driven from the establishment.

lines.japanese: 「いや、そりゃヘコみましたよ。まぁでもそのときは逆に心機一転かなって、ええそのときはね、ええそう思ったんすよ。ま、コレはきっかけだなー、やっぱオレはスタア目指すしかねえなー、とかって」
lines.english: “Yeah, that crushed me. But at the time, I thought maybe it was a fresh start. I really did. I thought, this is the push I needed. I've got no choice but to become a star now.”

lines.japanese: 水商売に見切りをつけたプラチナは、一大決心ののち、店に出入りしていた関係者の紹介でとあるＡＶプロダクションの門を叩いた。
lines.english: Turning his back on the nightlife business, Platinum made a momentous decision. Through an introduction from someone connected to his old club, he knocked on the door of a certain adult-video production company.

lines.japanese: 「ＮＥＷオレ様、文字通り裸一貫で再デビュー！　ってね、まあ、あんまひとには言えない道ですけど、一応自分的にはでっかい志を持って飛びこんだんすよ」
lines.english: “The brand-new me, making my debut with literally nothing but the skin on my back! It wasn't a path you could brag about, but in my own mind, I went in with huge ambitions.”

lines.japanese: しかし雛壇へ上がるための道が細く狭いのは、この世のどこに行ったって同じだ。コネもハナもない新人のプラチナに回ってくるのは、せいぜい企画ものビデオの汁男優ばかりだった。
lines.english: Yet wherever one went in this world, the ladder to a starring role was just as narrow. With neither connections nor star quality, the only work offered to a newcomer like Platinum was as a cum-shot extra in gimmick videos.

lines.japanese: ちなみに汁男優ってのは、ひとりの女優を大勢で取りかこみ一斉にあるものをぶっかける役どころらしい。
lines.english: For reference, such an extra's part apparently consisted of joining a crowd around a single actress and, all at once, covering her with a certain substance.

lines.japanese: たくさんのカメラや照明や人間の目に囲まれた中で、義務的に機械的に何か大切なものを絞りだして一発五千円。
lines.english: Surrounded by cameras, lights, and human eyes, he mechanically squeezed out something precious on command. Five thousand yen a shot.

lines.japanese: やがてプラチナは役者の仕事にしがみつく気力を失ってゆき、事務所の先輩に教わってスカウトの仕事を始めた。
lines.english: In time, Platinum lost the will to cling to acting. An older colleague at the agency taught him the trade, and he began working as a talent scout.

lines.japanese: 「だって汁男やっててもぜんぜん芸の肥やしにならないし、だったら──食ってく為だけだったら、べつに何の仕事だっていいわけじゃないすか」
lines.english: “Being a cum-shot extra wasn’t exactly feeding my craft. And if all I was doing was feeding myself—well, any job would do, wouldn’t it?”

lines.japanese: こうして夢のために働く青年は、わずか数年でただの働く青年になった。
lines.english: Thus, in only a few years, the young man working to support his dream became simply a working young man.

lines.japanese: そして現在にいたる、と。
lines.english: And that brought us to the present.

lines.japanese: 「まー、このお話の教訓は、貧乏人がヘタに金持っちゃいけないっていうね、ええ」
lines.english: “The moral is, poor people shouldn't get their hands on money. Yep.”

lines.japanese: 「おまえは本当に昔の話が好きだな」
lines.english: “You really do love talking about the old days.”

lines.japanese: メンマが俺の前に出来たてのラーメンを置いた。俺は無言で手を合わせて、割り箸を割った。
lines.english: Menma set a fresh bowl of ramen before me. I silently pressed my hands together, then snapped apart my disposable chopsticks.

lines.japanese: 「あはは、すいませんね！　毎度、口に出すことで発散してるんすよ！」
lines.english: “Ha ha, sorry! I get it out of my system by telling the story every time!”

lines.japanese: 「いいけどさ、もうちょっとこう、まとまりのある話になんねえの」
lines.english: “That's fine, but couldn't you give the story some kind of shape?”

lines.japanese: 俺はずるずる麺を啜りながら言った。
lines.english: I said it between noisy slurps of noodles.

lines.japanese: 「え、まとまりないすか？」
lines.english: “What, you mean it doesn't have one?”

lines.japanese: 「まとまりっつーか、オチがねえ救いがねえカタルシスがねえ。おまえさあ、ソレ、フィクションでいいから綺麗な後日談付けとけよ。なんかほら、めでたしめでたし的な」
lines.english: “Shape, ending—whatever. No punch line, no salvation, no catharsis. Even if you have to make it up, add a nice epilogue. You know. Happily ever after.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうすね！　そうっすよね！　付けられるといいっすよね！」
lines.english: “Ah, right! You're right! Sure would be nice if I had one to add!”

lines.japanese: プラチナは馬鹿みたいな高い声で言って、ばしばし俺の体を叩いた。それからひとり背中を丸めてくふふと笑う。気持ちの悪いやつだ。
lines.english: Platinum said it in an idiotically high voice and smacked me several times. Then he hunched forward and chuckled to himself. What a creep.

lines.japanese: 「ねえ、じゃあ、おふたりも昔の話してくださいよ」
lines.english: “Then why don't you two tell me about your pasts?”

lines.japanese: 「メンマ」
lines.english: “Menma.”

lines.japanese: 俺は自分に注目されるより早く、屋台の店主を促した。丼から目を離さずに食いつづける。
lines.english: Before the attention could settle on me, I prompted the cart's proprietor and kept eating without raising my eyes from the bowl.

lines.japanese: 「俺にはそんな面白い話はねえぞ」
lines.english: “I haven't got anything that interesting.”

lines.japanese: しかし語りたくないのはやつも同じみたいだった。
lines.english: Apparently he was no more eager to speak than I was.

lines.japanese: 「べつに、ラーメン屋や食の世界に憧れてこの道に入ったわけでもないしな。ただ働く歳になって働く場所を探してたとき、たまたま従業員募集のチラシを見つけて飛びこんだだけだ」
lines.english: “I didn't enter the trade out of any great love for ramen shops or the culinary world. I reached working age, went looking for somewhere to work, happened across a help-wanted flyer, and walked in.”

lines.japanese: 「でも、たまたまで始めたことが何年も続くって、それはそれで凄いことだろ」
lines.english: “But if something you started by accident lasts for years, that's impressive in its own right.”

lines.japanese: 重い口を軽くするため、俺はさりげなくメンマを持ちあげた。まあ、実際に思ったことではあるんだけど。
lines.english: To coax that heavy tongue into motion, I slipped in a little praise. I meant it, too.

lines.japanese: 「最初の一年は何度も辞めようと思ったけどな。だけど続けていくうちに、ラーメンを作ることと食わすことの中に少しずつ面白さが見えてきてな」
lines.english: “I thought about quitting plenty of times that first year. But as I kept at it, little by little I discovered what was interesting about making ramen and serving it to people.”

lines.japanese: 「自分の腕が上がっていく実感はあったし、長いこと店にいたから仕事仲間や常連客にもそれなりの愛着があったんだ。オヤジのシゴキはひどかったけどな」
lines.english: “I could feel myself improving. And after so long at the shop, I'd grown attached to my coworkers and regulars too. The old man's training was brutal, though.”

lines.japanese: 「オヤジって、え、父親？」
lines.english: “The old man? Your father?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、前の店の店長だ。俺たちはそう呼んでた。言ってみりゃ俺の師匠だな」
lines.english: “No, the manager at my old shop. That's what we called him. You might say he was my master.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、でも……たしかメンマさんの師匠って、めっちゃ厳しいひとだって言ってましたよね？」
lines.english: “Wait... didn't you say your master was incredibly strict?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ。それも、職人気質の芯の通った厳しさじゃなくてな。弟子を蔑んで自分の優位性に浸るような、そういう人間だった」
lines.english: “Yeah. It wasn't the principled severity of a craftsman, either. He looked down on his apprentices and savored the power he had over them.”

lines.japanese: 「マジすか！　最低なヤローっすねそいつ。料理が上手いぐらいで何様のつもりっすか」
lines.english: “Seriously? What a piece of shit. Who did he think he was just because he could cook?”

lines.japanese: 「王様なんだよ。それは仕方ない、腕だけがすべての世界だからな。たしかな腕を持っていたオヤジは、あの店じゃ文句なしに王様だった。それについちゃあ俺たちだって、愚痴はこぼすが異論はなかった」
lines.english: “The king. No helping it. Skill was everything in that world. The old man unquestionably had it, so inside that shop, he was king. We complained, but none of us disputed the crown.”

lines.japanese: メンマはちらりと後ろを向いて、自分用の丸椅子を引きずりよせた。その上に、鈍牛みたいな巨体が重々しく腰を沈めた。
lines.english: Menma glanced behind him and dragged over his own stool. His massive, oxlike frame settled heavily onto it.

lines.japanese: 客の前じゃ滅多に座らない男がどうしたんだろう。もしかしたら今夜は話をしたい気分なのかもしれない。
lines.english: The man almost never sat in front of customers. What had got into him? Maybe tonight he wanted to talk.

lines.japanese: 「メンマ」
lines.english: “Menma.”

lines.japanese: 俺はプラチナから注がれた酒を、そのまま店主の方へ移動させた。やつは目で礼を述べた。俺はラーメンを食いながら続ける。
lines.english: I slid the sake Platinum had poured me toward the proprietor. He thanked me with his eyes. I went on eating.

lines.japanese: 「そういやおまえ、前にそのオヤジを殴ったから破門になったって言ってたよな」
lines.english: “Come to think of it, you said the old man threw you out after you hit him.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ」
lines.english: “Yeah.”

lines.japanese: 「うーん、でもそれ、未だに信じらンないんすけど。だって、メンマさんがキレるなんて余程のことでしょ。そのおっさん、そんなひどいシゴキ野郎だったんすか」
lines.english: “Still, I can hardly believe it. It'd take something serious to make you snap. Was the guy really that abusive?”

lines.japanese: メンマは俺が譲った酒を一口で飲みほした。体格に見合った見事な飲みっぷりだった。
lines.english: Menma drained the sake I’d passed him in a single gulp. He drank with a gusto worthy of his size.

lines.japanese: 「その店に、よく四、五人で食いにくるやんちゃなガキ共がいたんだ。近所の学校の制服だった」
lines.english: “Four or five rowdy kids used to come eat at the shop. Uniforms from a school nearby.”

lines.japanese: それからメンマは淡々と、しかし、いつになく長いこと喋りつづけた。
lines.english: Then Menma began to speak—flatly, but at far greater length than usual.

lines.japanese: ──放課後にやってくるツッパリ少年たち。
lines.english: —A pack of teenage toughs coming in after school.

lines.japanese: その金だの茶だののカラフルな頭の中に、ひとりだけ真っ黒い髪のやつがいたらしい。同級生たちが遠慮なく騒いでいても、ひとりだけ下を向いて静かにラーメンを食っている、そんなやつだったという。
lines.english: Amid all those heads dyed gold and brown, there was apparently one boy with solid black hair. His classmates made all the noise they liked, while he alone kept his eyes down and quietly ate his ramen.

lines.japanese: そいつは店に入ってくるときも店を出ていくときも、いつもいちばんケツを歩いてた。だから会計はいつもそいつがひとりで済ませていた。立て替え代をあとで徴収してたのか、もちろんメンマには知りようもない。
lines.english: Entering or leaving, that boy always walked at the very back. So he always settled the bill alone. Whether he collected their shares afterward, Menma naturally had no way to know.

lines.japanese: 茶髪のガキ共はラーメンを食う最初から最後まで、この店は遅いだの臭いだのとデカい声で言いたい放題だ。でも黒いやつだけは、金を払うとき、必ずごちそうさまでしたと頭を下げていった。
lines.english: From first bite to last, the brown-haired punks loudly complained that the service was slow, the place stank, and whatever else occurred to them. But when the black-haired one paid, he never failed to bow and thank them for the meal.

lines.japanese: 「ある夜、いつもしんがりで入ってくるはずのそいつが、先頭に立って店へやって来たんだ。後ろに連れていたのは、どことなく似た顔をしたおかっぱ頭の女の子だった」
lines.english: “One night, the boy who always came in at the rear walked into the shop at the very front. Behind him was a girl with a bob cut who looked vaguely like him.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、その少年の妹っすね」
lines.english: “Ah. His little sister.”

lines.japanese: たぶんな、とメンマは言った。
lines.english: Probably, Menma said.

lines.japanese: テーブルが埋まっていて、兄妹はカウンター席に並んで座った。ラーメンを届けると、妹は美味しいと顔をほころばせながら不器用に箸を進めた。兄貴は自分が見つけた店だと言って得意そうだった。
lines.english: The tables were full, so brother and sister sat side by side at the counter. When their ramen arrived, the sister worked her chopsticks clumsily, her face opening into a smile as she called it delicious. Her brother proudly announced that he'd discovered the place.

lines.japanese: 妹は何故こんなに美味しいのかと兄貴に訊いた。兄貴は答えに窮して周囲をうかがった。メンマは壁の張り紙を指した。兄貴はぺこりと頭を下げてから、妹にそれを読んできかせた。動物系＋魚介系の自家製Ｗスープ！
lines.english: She asked why it tasted so good. Her brother, at a loss, looked around for help. Menma pointed to a notice on the wall. The boy bobbed his head in thanks, then read it aloud to her: *Homemade double broth—meat and seafood!*

lines.japanese: だが妹は好奇心旺盛な年頃だった。さらにＷスープとは何かと尋ねた。兄貴の視線がいま一度巨体の店員に助けを求めた。
lines.english: But his sister was at an inquisitive age. Next she asked what double broth meant. Once again, the brother's eyes appealed to the enormous employee.

lines.japanese: メンマはカウンターに身を乗りだして幼い客と目線を揃え、まるでおとぎ話でも聞かせるみたいに、ゆっくりとひとつずつ使っている素材の名を挙げていった。
lines.english: Menma leaned across the counter until his eyes were level with his young customer, then slowly named each ingredient, one by one, as if telling her a fairy tale.

lines.japanese: 動物系はトンコツ、トンソク、牛テール、トリガラ、モミジ。魚介系は鮭とば、いりこ、さば、カツオ、するめ、コンブ、それから──
lines.english: The animal broth: pork bones, trotters, oxtail, chicken carcasses, chicken feet. The seafood: dried salmon, sardines, mackerel, bonito, dried squid, dried kelp, and then—

lines.japanese: 「そこでいきなり、大人げない怒声が俺の耳に浴びせられた。馬鹿野郎だか脳足りんだか、そんなようなガキでも知ってる単純な侮蔑語だった。兄妹はまるで自分が怒鳴られたみたいに固まった」
lines.english: “Without warning, an adult’s angry bellow cut in. Idiot, moron—some simple insult even a child would know. The brother and sister froze as if he’d shouted at them.”

lines.japanese: 「オヤジはヒステリックな声で俺を罵倒しはじめた。たしかに俺がしたことは重要機密の漏洩だ。やつにはその権利があったと思う」
lines.english: “The old man began abusing me in a hysterical voice. Admittedly, I had divulged a vital trade secret. I suppose he had cause.”

lines.japanese: 「でも美味しい美味しいと無邪気に微笑んでいたガキ共が、カウンターテーブル一枚挟んだほんの数十センチ先にいるんだ。何もそんな場所で爆発することはないと俺は思った」
lines.english: “But the children who’d been innocently smiling and calling the food delicious were barely two feet away, with only the counter between us. I thought there was no need to explode right there.”

lines.japanese: 「汚らわしい言葉が飛びつづける。俺にとっては他愛もない日常茶飯事だが、兄妹の箸は止まっていた。俺はやめてくださいと言った。オヤジに逆らったのは、神にかけてそれが初めてだった」
lines.english: “The filth kept flying. I heard that kind of thing every day and thought nothing of it, but the siblings’ chopsticks had stopped. I asked him to stop. God is my witness, it was the first time I’d ever defied the old man.”

lines.japanese: 「オヤジは御玉で沸騰した湯をすくって俺の体にぶちまけた。俺はその温度に悲鳴をあげそうになったが、兄妹が怯えていたから、堪えてもう一度やめてくださいと言った」
lines.english: “The old man dipped a ladle into the boiling water and flung it over me. The heat nearly tore a scream out of me, but the children were frightened, so I held it in and asked him again to stop.”

lines.japanese: 「オヤジは口答えするなと逆上して、俺の足元に丼を叩きつけた。瀬戸物の割れる音が店じゅうに響いた。兄貴は青ざめたように俯き、妹はいまにも泣きだしそうだった。俺は静かにやめろと言った」
lines.english: “Enraged that I’d answered back, he smashed a bowl at my feet. Breaking porcelain rang through the restaurant. The brother went white and looked down; the sister looked ready to cry. Quietly, I told him to stop.”

lines.japanese: 「オヤジは乱暴に俺の頭を掴み、どこかへ──ごぼごぼ泡立つ寸胴の中だったかもしれない──どこかへ叩きつけようとした。俺はやつの腕を振りほどき、やめろと言って中年太りの腹に重いのを一発埋めこんだ」
lines.english: “The old man seized my head and tried to slam it somewhere—perhaps into the great stockpot bubbling beside us. I tore loose, told him to stop, and buried one heavy punch in his middle-aged gut.”

lines.japanese: 「そのまま、おとなしくなったオヤジの体を引きずって、店の外に放りだした。やつは尻餅をつきながらクビだ出ていけと喚いた。俺はお世話になりましたと頭を下げ、その場で白衣を脱ぎすてた……」
lines.english: “Then I dragged the suddenly docile old man outside and threw him into the street. Sitting on his ass, he screamed that I was fired and ordered me out. I bowed, thanked him for everything, and stripped off my white chef's coat on the spot...”

lines.japanese: メンマは大きな息をついた。一升瓶を掴んで自分のグラスに溢れるほど注ぐ。
lines.english: Menma drew a great breath. He seized the large sake bottle and filled his glass to overflowing.

lines.japanese: 次の言葉を待っている俺たちの前で、やつは喋りすぎた喉を潤すように一息で半分以上空けた。
lines.english: As we waited for what came next, he emptied more than half in one breath, as though soothing a throat dried by more talking than he was used to.

lines.japanese: 「……ああ、悪いなドラ、この話にもオチや救いはないんだ。ただの喧嘩っぱやいろくでなしが、考えなしに暴れて挫折しただけの物語だ」
lines.english: “...Sorry, Dra. This story has no ending or salvation either. Just a hotheaded bum who lashed out without thinking and fell flat on his face.”

lines.japanese: 大男はそんな冗談で昔話を締めた。そして残った酒を一口ずつ飲みはじめた。
lines.english: The giant closed his story with the joke, then began drinking the rest one sip at a time.

lines.japanese: 「いや！　きっと救われてますよ！」
lines.english: “No! I'm sure someone was saved!”

lines.japanese: 「その少年、きっとメンマさんの行動に心打たれて、強いものに立ちむかう勇気をもらったはずです！　そうっすよ、間違いないっすよ！」
lines.english: “That boy must have been moved by what you did. You gave him the courage to stand against someone stronger! You did. I know it!”

lines.japanese: プラチナがこぶしを握りしめて理想的な後日談をでっち上げた。まさか。青春ドラマじゃあるまいし、そんな安直なご都合主義がまかりとおるはずはない。
lines.english: Platinum clenched his fist and made up the perfect epilogue on the spot. Impossible. This wasn’t some youth drama. Reality didn’t permit contrivances that cheap.

lines.japanese: でも、ちょっと信じてみたくなる話だ。
lines.english: Still, it was a story I almost wanted to believe.

lines.japanese: 「かもな」
lines.english: “Maybe.”

lines.japanese: そう言って、俺はぬるくなった水をプラチナの酒に打ちあわせた。かちん。
lines.english: I said it and clinked my lukewarm water against Platinum's sake.

lines.japanese: 「ドラ」
lines.english: “Dra.”

lines.japanese: 角刈りの店主は乾杯に参加せず、腕を組んで薄く笑っていた。
lines.english: The crew-cut proprietor did not join our toast. Arms folded, he wore a faint smile.

lines.japanese: 「最後はおまえの番だ」
lines.english: “You're last.”

lines.japanese: 「え……ああ」
lines.english: “Ah... right.”

lines.japanese: 参った。
lines.english: I was in trouble.

lines.japanese: 重い口を割って古傷を垣間見せてくれた男に、茶化しや虚言で応えたくはないが──俺の身の上を偽らず語るには、タカシや鷲介のことを避けるわけにいかない。
lines.english: A man had overcome his reluctance and shown us one of his old wounds. I didn’t want to answer that with jokes or lies—but I couldn’t speak truthfully about my life without Takashi and Shusuke.

lines.japanese: しかしその辺のことは、メンマの師匠のレシピ以上に重大な機密事項だ。そりゃそうだろ。まだ、おまえにさえ話してないことがたくさんあるってのに。
lines.english: And those things were secrets more vital than his master's recipe. Of course they were. There was still so much I hadn't told even you.

lines.japanese: 「そうだな……」
lines.english: “Let's see...”

lines.japanese: 俺は傾けた丼の縁に唇を浸してから、慎重に、偽りではない言葉を選びながら口を開いた。
lines.english: I rested my lips against the rim of the tilted bowl. Then I began, carefully choosing words I could say without lying.

lines.japanese: 「俺には、その、兄弟同然に育ったやつらがいるんだ」
lines.english: “There are people I grew up with who are practically my brothers.”

lines.japanese: 「兄弟、同然……？」
lines.english: “Practically... your brothers?”

lines.japanese: 「そう……ま、妹分もひとりいるんだけど、それは置いとこう。いまは男兄弟の話をする」
lines.english: “Yeah. There's a girl who's like a little sister too, but leave her aside. I'm talking about the brothers.”

lines.japanese: 箸を置いて、水を一口飲んだ。
lines.english: I set down my chopsticks and drank a mouthful of water.

lines.japanese: 「俺はいちばん下、まあ、言うなれば末っ子だな」
lines.english: “I'm the youngest. The baby of the family, you might say.”

lines.japanese: 「長男は……自閉症とでも言うのかな、もう永いことずっと自分の世界に引きこもってて。ぶっちゃけ、遠い国に行ったきり帰ってこない故人みてえなもん」
lines.english: “The eldest is... autistic, I guess you’d call it. He’s spent years and years shut away in his own world. Honestly, he’s like a dead man who traveled to a distant country and never came home.”

lines.japanese: 「三男は俺と同じで、ふらふらバイトして食いつないでるやつ。生まれた時期的に言や、俺とは双子みたいなもんだから、兄貴っつうより遠慮のいらない悪友みたいな感覚で」
lines.english: “The third son is a serial part-timer scraping by from job to job, same as me. Going by when we were born, we’re practically twins, so he feels less like an older brother than an old partner in crime I never have to stand on ceremony with.”

lines.japanese: 「こいつはいつもへらへら笑ってて、他人の顔色ばっか窺いながら生きてるいけ好かねえ野郎だけど、正直やつのおべんちゃらで俺らが救われたことは何度もあった、っつうカンジ」
lines.english: “He’s an obnoxious bastard, always grinning, always watching people’s faces. But honestly, his sweet talk has saved our asses more times than I can count. Something like that.”

lines.japanese: 「上から二番目のやつはいちばん真面目だ。真面目すぎてどうかとも思うけど、でもわりと尊敬してる。いろんな意味で強ええやつなんだ」
lines.english: “The second is the most serious. Too serious for his own good, if you ask me, but I respect him. He's strong in all kinds of ways.”

lines.japanese: 「やつにとっちゃ面白くもないはずなのに、ちゃんと毎日学校に行ってる。たまに逃げだすことはあるけど、一晩眠れば綺麗さっぱり忘れてまた学校へ通う。気の毒だけど偉いって思うよ」
lines.english: “He goes to school every day, though it can't be any fun for him. Sometimes he runs away, but one night's sleep wipes it clean and he goes right back. I feel sorry for him. I admire him too.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、あのすいません。えっとー、兄弟同然に育ったってことは……つまり、みんな隣近所に住んでるってことすかね？」
lines.english: “Ah, sorry. When you say you grew up like brothers... do you mean you all live in the same neighborhood?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、まあ、そんなとこ。近くにはいるんだけど、会うことはほとんどない──みたいな？」
lines.english: “Yeah, more or less. We're nearby, but almost never see one another... something like that?”

lines.japanese: 「ふぅーん」
lines.english: “Hmmm.”

lines.japanese: 「そんで、俺とへらへらの三男坊は……ま、ちょっと格好いい言い方をさせてもらうなら、二番目の兄貴を陰ながら応援してるっつーのかな。いや、勝手に期待を押しつけてるとも言うんだけどさ」
lines.english: “So the grinning third son and I... if you’ll let me make it sound a little noble, I suppose we quietly cheer the second brother on from the sidelines. Though you could also say we pile our hopes on him without asking.”

lines.japanese: 「はっ。なんせ長男ヒッキーだし、俺ら双子は将来の展望もねーしだ。そりゃ仕方ない、俺らの希望の受け皿はあいつしかいねえんだ。あいつに独り立ちしてもらわねと……なんてーか、いろいろ不都合があってさ」
lines.english: “Hah. The eldest is a shut-in, and we twins have no future to speak of. Can’t be helped: the second brother is the only one left to carry our hopes. We need him to stand on his own someday... or, let’s just say, it causes problems.”

lines.japanese: 「だから、いずれ時期が来るまでに……俺らもその、知識と経験？　っつうの？　あと多少は金もさ、貯めといてやって」
lines.english: “So before that day comes... we’re trying to bank some knowledge and experience for him, I guess you’d call it. A little money too.”

lines.japanese: 「で、やつが社会に羽ばたくっつーときに、俺らの持ってるもん全部渡せたらなあ、とかまあ、そんな風に思ってるわけよ」
lines.english: “Then, when he’s ready to go out into the world, maybe we can hand him everything we’ve got. That’s more or less what we think.”

lines.japanese: 俺は顔を上げてメンマとプラチナを見た。どっちも唇を結んで真剣に聞いていた。なんだかもどかしくて、後ろ頭をがしがし掻いた。
lines.english: I looked up at Menma and Platinum. Both listened intently, lips pressed shut. Frustrated by how little I’d managed to say, I scratched hard at the back of my head.

lines.japanese: 「あー、ごめん、とりあえずこれで終わりなんすけど」
lines.english: “Ah, sorry. That's the end, for now.”

lines.japanese: 「へ？　あ、そうなんだ」
lines.english: “Huh? Oh. Is it?”

lines.japanese: 「かぁー、やっぱ分かんねえよなあ、こんな話じゃ」
lines.english: “God, of course you can't make sense of a story like that.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、まあ……」
lines.english: “Mm. Well...”

lines.japanese: ラーメン屋とスカウトマンは口を縦に細く開けたような表情で、いま自らの取るべき反応を探っているように見えた。
lines.english: The ramen man and the scout wore identical expressions, mouths hanging open in the same narrow vertical shapes as they searched for the response expected of them.

lines.japanese: 「んー、なんて言うんすかね……理解は出来ないけど納得はできたような？」
lines.english: “Hmm. How do I put it? I don’t understand, exactly, but I think I get it?”

lines.japanese: 「事情は複雑だけど確たる信念がある。そういうことだろ、ドラ」
lines.english: “The circumstances are tangled, but you know what you believe in. Is that it, Dra?”

lines.japanese: 「悪い……いつか話せるときが来たら話すよ」
lines.english: “Sorry... If the time ever comes when I can tell you, I will.”

lines.japanese: 「何を？」
lines.english: “Tell them what?”
“Ah.”

lines.japanese: 割りこんできた声に振りかえった。パル姐さんとあいつ……鳴がいた。
lines.english: I turned toward the voice cutting in. Paru was there, and with her... Naru.

lines.japanese: 「おう。いらっしゃい」
lines.english: “Hey. Welcome.”

lines.japanese: 「おーす、喜べオトコ共ー！　おばちゃん今日は、若いギャル、ナンパしてきちゃったよー！」
lines.english: “Hey, rejoice, men! This old lady went and picked up a young gal tonight!”

lines.japanese: 「こ、こんばんはっ」
lines.english: “G-good evening.”

lines.japanese: 「きゃっほー、ナイス、パルさーん！　ギャール！　ギャール！」
lines.english: “All right! Nice one, Paru! A giiirl! A giiirl!”

lines.japanese: 「ハッ、なにがギャルだ。ただのジャリじゃねーか、おまえらちょっと──」
lines.english: “Hah. What girl? She's a kid. You people need to—”

lines.japanese: 「ねーねー、それ蒼穹女学院の制服でしょ？　いいね、お嬢っぽいね。肌きれーだしね。キミひょっとしてヨーロッパの血入ってない？　いいよいいよー、キミさ、ちょっと社会勉強兼ねたアルバイトに興味ない？」
lines.english: “Hey, hey, that's the Misora Girls' Academy uniform, right? Nice. Very refined. Beautiful skin too. Any European blood in you, maybe? Good, good. Say, interested in a part-time job that gives you a little real-world education?”

lines.japanese: 「あ！　ちょ、ストップストップ！　うっそ、キミ驚いた顔ちょー可愛くない？　よく言われるでしょ？　言われるって絶対！　ででで、その魅力を最大限活かせる仕事があったらどうする？　話だけでも聞いとく？」
lines.english: “Ah! Wait, stop! No way—isn't your surprised face insanely cute? People must tell you all the time. I know they do! So, so, so, what if there were a job that used that charm to the fullest? Want to hear the pitch?”

lines.japanese: 「え、や、あのう……」
lines.english: “Um, no, I...”

lines.japanese: 「なーんてね！　あはは、うそうそ。僕、オンとオフは混同しない主義なの。いまのはほんの名刺代わりね、そーゆー仕事してますっていう。あ、でも可愛いって言ったのは本当──」
lines.english: “Just kidding! Ha ha, kidding. I make it a rule not to mix work and private life. Think of that as my business card—just showing you what I do. Though I meant the part about you being cute—”

lines.japanese: 「──あれ、どしたんすかドラさん、そんな恐いカオしちゃって」
lines.english: “—Huh? What's wrong, Dra? That's a scary face.”

lines.japanese: 「う、うっせーな、俺はいつでも恐いカオしてるっつーの。ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ。ブッ殺すぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Sh-shut up. My face is always scary. I'll fucking kill you, asshole. I'll fucking kill you, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「プラチナ。あんた、あたしと初対面のときはそんな自己アピールなかったじゃないか」
lines.english: “Platinum. You didn't give *me* that pitch when we first met.”

lines.japanese: 「え……そ、そうでしたっけ？」
lines.english: “What...? D-didn't I?”

lines.japanese: 「ほー、あたしゃ記憶にすら残らない女か」
lines.english: “Oh-ho. So forgettable I didn’t even stick in your memory, am I?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、はは……いえ、パルさんそんな風に見えなかったって言うか……」
lines.english: “Ah, ha ha... no. I mean, you didn't seem like that sort of woman...”

lines.japanese: 「ああッ？　じゃあ何かい、あたしの顔は客取れるように見えないってかい」
lines.english: “Oh? You saying I don’t look like I could pull customers?”

lines.japanese: 「や、外見っていうかその、滲みでる歳が……」
lines.english: “No, it’s not your looks, exactly. It’s more... the age showing through...”
“My age!?”

lines.japanese: 「そ、それよりパルさん！　ほら、早くそちらのお嬢さん紹介してくださいよ！」
lines.english: “M-more importantly, Paru! Hurry and introduce this young lady!”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうか」
lines.english: “Oh. Right.”

lines.japanese: パルさんは立ったまま、鳴とプラチナをそれぞれに紹介した。
lines.english: Still standing, Paru introduced Naru and Platinum to each other.

lines.japanese: 人見知りする小娘は、いかにも遊び人風のやさ男に堅くるしいおじぎをした。ひと懐っこいやさ男は、堅くるしいおじぎをした小娘に手慣れた笑顔を返した。
lines.english: The shy girl gave the obvious playboy a stiff, formal bow. The affable playboy returned it with a practiced smile.

lines.japanese: 「ままっ、立ち話もなんですから。ねっ、ふたりとも座ってくださいよ──っても、あー、四人は無理か」
lines.english: “Come on, let’s not stand around talking. Both of you, sit down—though, ah, four won’t fit.”

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、ちょいとあんた、向こう行っとくれよ」
lines.english: “Dra, move over there, will you?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　お、俺かよ」
lines.english: “What? M-me?”

lines.japanese: パルさんは路上に据えられたテーブルを指しながら、三人がけのカウンター席から俺の体を引きはがした。
lines.english: Pointing toward the table set out on the street, Paru peeled me away from the three-seat counter.

lines.japanese: 「鳴、ドラが寂しがるからあんたもあっち」
lines.english: “Naru, Dra will get lonely, so you go over there too.”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、ひでぇー、俺ら除けモンかよ」
lines.english: “Wow, that's cold. We're being cast out?”

lines.japanese: 「仕方ないだろ。ここ全員は並べないんだし、かと言って全員でテーブル行っちまったら、今度はメンマが可哀想じゃないか」
lines.english: “Can't be helped. We can't all line up here, and if everyone moves to the table, poor Menma gets left behind.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ。俺は体こそでかいが、心はドラと同じぐらい小さいからな」
lines.english: “True. My body may be large, but my heart is every bit as small as Dra's.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえよ角刈り。てめ、頭のカドっこ丸くすんぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Shut up, crew cut. I'll round the corners off your head, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 俺は不服そうなふりをしながら、パルさんに席を譲ってテーブルへ向かった。あとから鳴がちょこちょこ付いてくる。
lines.english: Pretending to be aggrieved, I surrendered my seat to Paru and headed for the table. Naru pattered after me.

lines.japanese: なぜだか俺は落ちつかない気分だった。
lines.english: For some reason, I couldn't settle down.
